source_review.notes: Checked all nine structured references at dbt Labs, Apache Iceberg, Debezium, PostgreSQL, Apache Beam, and OpenLineage; every URL returned HTTP 200. Claims about dbt incremental filters, unique keys, strategies, schema-change limitations, and full refresh; Iceberg append-only incremental reads and atomic snapshot publication; PostgreSQL/Debezium ordering, transaction boundaries, deletes, tombstones, and possible duplicate delivery; Beam watermarks and lateness; and OpenLineage run/job/dataset identity match the cited documentation and remain product/version scoped.

evidence: Checked source state S_c, full transformation F_v, prior trusted output O_a, ordered change interval Delta_(a,b], reference states R_a/R_b, incremental transition U_v, influence relation I_v(x), and affected set A_v(Delta) for stable meanings.

Checked the full-equivalence obligation, checkpoint/publication transition, affected-set union, occurrence identity, entity version, event time, source position, and visible tombstone-filtered state for coherent notation.
Draft chapter validation accepted the exact front matter, H1, H2/H3 contract, local links, and GitHub-compatible inline/display math.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Business time, source cursor, entity version, delivery identity, target generation, and transformation version remain explicitly separated.

evidence: Executed the annotated finite model: 3 initial rows, 5 delivered changes, 4 unique changes, checkpoint 3 advancing to 7, and visible state o1=150, o3=250, o4=50.
Recomputed both incremental and independent full-replay totals as 450 cents and verified replaying the identical interval leaves state unchanged.
Recomputed the naive business-time filter: only o4 is selected, stale o1/o2/o3 remain, and total is 650 cents.
Recomputed Exercise 3: a correction to source day 20 affects output days 20 through 26, requiring source context days 14 through 26 for direct seven-day recomputation.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All explicit row counts, cursor values, totals, replay results, delete visibility, and window boundaries reproduce exactly.

evidence: Verified the equivalence equation is conditional on a trusted prior output, a complete ordered change interval, matching transformation/reference versions, and a declared output equivalence relation.
Verified affected outputs are the union of influence sets for changed source keys; row-local modified-time selection is insufficient for joins, aggregates, windows, reference changes, and deletes.

Verified half-open cursor interval (a,b] composes without gaps or overlap when source identity/epoch and ordering are stable, while inclusive timestamp fallback requires identity-aware deduplication or exact replacement.
Verified checkpoint advancement before trusted publication permits loss and publication without a bound checkpoint makes retry outcome ambiguous.
Verified associative sufficient state can support incremental aggregates, while non-invertible or order-sensitive calculations require retained components or affected-region recomputation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The deductions state completeness, ordering, identity, influence, algebra, and commit premises rather than attributing correctness to an incremental strategy name.

evidence: Reviewed empty intervals, first build, full refresh, equal timestamps, clock regressions, timestamp precision, nullable/nonunique keys, duplicates, out-of-order changes, version ties, source epochs, and retention gaps.
Reviewed inserts, updates, deletes, tombstones, primary-key changes, before/after images, transaction boundaries, bootstrap-to-stream handoff, crash redelivery, and poison/conflicting events.
Reviewed late/unbounded data, lookback edges, aggregate group moves, distinct/min/max, window halos, sessions, many-to-many joins, mutable dimensions, and transitive downstream influence.

Reviewed concurrent writers, stale-base commits, ambiguous acknowledgements, destination pruning, partial output, schema/code/runtime/reference changes, rollback, rebuild horizon, tenancy, and sensitive CDC history.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The ten examples and five exercises cover temporal, identity, state-transition, dependency, concurrency, migration, security, and recovery boundaries.

evidence: Checked that prior output/checkpoint/version form one trusted generation and that source intervals bind cursor bounds, source identity/epoch, transaction semantics, and retention evidence.
Checked stable occurrence identity, entity key, operation, ordering/version, schema, delete behavior, deterministic duplicate/conflict resolution, and non-resurrection of tombstones.
Checked affected-set closure through joins, aggregates, windows, references, code, schema, and downstream models, with destination pruning separated from source completeness.

Checked isolated candidate construction, idempotent replay, quality gates, conditional publication, authoritative reconciliation of unknown outcomes, and checkpoint advancement only with the validated generation.
Checked periodic full differential comparison, raw-history rebuildability, lag/lateness/drift SLOs, lineage, access control, retention, rollback, and recovery drills.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariants cover source discovery through canonical state transition and dependency propagation to one published, recoverable model generation.

evidence: Reviewed the full-equivalence obligation and confirmed that a successful delta job proves only its transition, not equality with F_v(S_b), unless interval and affected-set completeness premises hold.
Reviewed the counterexample in which old-business-time updates and a delete are omitted; the resulting 650 total differs from the correct/full 450 total despite a plausible successful run.
Reviewed duplicate replay: stable event identity suppresses the repeated o1 change, entity version prevents older state from winning, and the tombstone prevents o2 resurrection.
Reviewed the trailing-window influence proof: source day 20 belongs to each seven-day frame ending from day 20 through day 26, so output-day-only selection is incomplete.
Reviewed stale-base concurrency: compare-and-swap rejects B after A publishes, requiring B to rebase from generation 51 before conditionally publishing generation 52.
proof_review.notes: Each proof distinguishes logical equivalence from source-delivery guarantees, implementation strategy, operational evidence, and performance optimization.

evidence: The equivalence equation is explicitly presented as an obligation under declared premises, not a universal theorem about incremental execution.
Lookback is labeled a bounded operational policy rather than proof against all future late arrivals.
Affected-set and sufficient-state reasoning identify when recomputation is required rather than claiming every model has a compact inverse.
dbt, Iceberg, Debezium, PostgreSQL, Beam, and OpenLineage behavior is source-attributed and implementation/version scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter visibly separates mathematical conditions, source contracts, vendor mechanisms, empirical operating limits, and recommended controls.

evidence: The finite executable model is explicitly limited to ordered in-memory changes and disclaims real log retention, transactions, distributed concurrency, schema evolution, and publication protocols.
Full-refresh comparison is treated as sampled/differential evidence whose independence and source cut must be controlled, not infallible proof by name.
Lookback duration, reconciliation cadence, state retention, and scan/write cost are described as workload/SLO-dependent decisions requiring observed lateness and recovery evidence.
Production acceptance requires source controls, key/set/value differences, delete evidence, checkpoint-generation identity, drift monitoring, rollback, and recovery drills.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Executable demonstration, algebraic reasoning, documentation-derived claims, and deployed-system evidence each retain an explicit scope.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distinctions among full state/delta; business event time/source cursor/entity version; occurrence identity/business key; delivery duplicate/legitimate repeated value; tombstone/physical absence; source filtering/destination pruning; append/upsert/replace/recompute; late data/out-of-order delivery; checkpoint/output generation; schema synchronization/historical backfill; and incremental read/full change semantics.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable cursor contracts, source epochs/retention alarms, CDC canonicalization, stable IDs and versions, affected-set planning, merge/delete handling, aggregate/window recomputation, bounded lookback, isolated candidates, compare-and-swap publication, ambiguous-outcome reconciliation, full differential validation, versioned migrations, observability, security, rollback, and rebuild drills.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review establishes full equivalence, source-native cursors, affected sets, and atomic checkpoint publication; exposition progresses from source/change semantics through state transitions, dependency propagation, concurrency, version changes, validation, and operations; the executable counterexample makes silent timestamp loss concrete; and ten examples plus five solved exercises combine calculation and design.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. References and local checks were performed on 2026-09-02. The finite standard-library model and recomputations do not establish production source-log completeness, transaction/snapshot handoff, cursor retention, clock/precision policy, CDC connector behavior, stable identity/version quality, delete/tombstone retention, arbitrary dependency influence, aggregate/window invertibility, distributed ordering/concurrency, destination-merge correctness, engine-specific incremental-read coverage, schema/code/reference migrations, atomic catalog publication, tenant/privacy compliance, lineage completeness, cost/latency SLOs, rollback, or disaster recovery; those require system-specific deployed evidence.
